   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From:Stephen Watson, E. KILBRIDE



Dear Ron and Brian,

Re: Mike Jones' letter in Issue
38, why bother with TASCON when
with the assistance of the
manual and OUTLET you can
produce an excellent version of
TASWORD 2 to run with the Plus
D. I recently purchased TASWORD
2 and followed the instructions
in the manual for the conversion
to the microdrive version then
ran the TAS-EXTRAS programme in
OUTLET Issue 24.This should also
meet J.W. Tollets' requirements
(MORE MAIL, Issue 36).


As a follow up to my recent
letter regarding thermal paper
for the Brother HRS printer, I
have been looking into alter-
natives. I have found that paper
for FAX machines gives perfectly
acceptable results, as you can
see from this letter printed out
on it, and if you have a friend/
relative who works for a company
whose office would be willing to
sell you a roll from their next
order,it can be relatively cheap
- around `8 a 100-metre roll.

    Keep up the good work!

         Stephen Watson


Thanks, Stephen. - Brian Cavers

From: Peter Wright, HUDDERSFIELD

Query: I use a TANDY TRS 80 Line
printer V11 which has graphics,
dot-addressable,7 or 8 BIT ASCII
serial on 8 BIT ASCII Parallel.
Any ideas how to obtain graphics
for Spectrum via LLprint III,
please? I can't locate any code.

            Peter

If the TANDY is Epson-compatible
use LPRINT CHR$ 0;CHR$ 3 which
should show a menu at the bottom
of the screen. Press ENTER. If
you have no luck, try HANDYDUMP
(OUTLET 27). Alter line  9780 to
LPRINT CHR$ 5;:GO SUB 9795 and
use the OPUS option. Write again
if you need more help.
                  - Brian Cavers

From: R. Bates, NOTTINGHAM

Dear Ron,
Thank you for the safe delivery
of Back Issue No.9 which I
wanted mainly for the game of
LIFE. This is a splendid version
of Conway's classic especially
in having such a large grid.

However,the pixel-sized cells do
make it very difficult to plot
the initial LIFEFORMS accurately
and to discern precisely what is
going on during the evolution of
the LIFE FORMS.

Fortunately, it is possible to
save and reload screens once the
LIFEFORM has been plotted or at
any time during its evolution.

This is achieved by BREAKing to
BASIC and entering the SAVE/LOAD
SCREEN$ command appropriate to
the storage medium. Disciple
users can just snap the screen.
The evolution can be restarted
by entering GOTO 17 (not RUN).

The ability to LOAD Screens into
LIFE makes it possible to pre-
pare LIFEFORMS with the benefit
of the magnification function in
ARTIST 2 or ARTSTUDIO. The 8 x
magnification of ARTSTUDIO with
its pixel-grid, is particularly
useful.

Magnification of the LIFEFORM in
this way also makes it possible
to examine details of its
evolution in successively-saved
screens.

CLIP COMPOSER can be used to
extract interesting LIFEFORMS
from the clutter on-screen.

If the original author, Paul
Hiley, is still in contact with
OUTLET, would it be possible to
make the following modifications
to the program?

a)To eliminate wrap-round on all
margins. Re-incarnation of LIFE-
FORMS which should have dropped
from the known universe can
seriously disrupt the evolution
of the more complex life format-
ions. At present it is necessary
to erase LIFE FORMS as they wrap
round.

b) To provide pixel co-ordinates
of the cursor in plot mode.

c) To provide a magnification
routine.

d) To provide an option for
quarter character size cells.

e) Choice of generation time.

All, or any, of these modificat-
ions would help to make OUTLIFE
the ultimate version for the
SPECTRUM.
            R. BATES

We've not heard from Paul for a
long time now which is a shame
as he contributed some fine
programs. Unfortunately,it would
be a big project for anyone else
to attempt to modify a machine
code program like OUTLIFE.
                  - Brian Cavers

From Raymond Hoy, BASINGSTOKE



Dear Brian & Ron,

I wonder if you or any of your
readers can help me track down a
scanner to go with my set-up,
which is a Spectrum+ (128) with
a Disciple attached and an Epson
compatible printer.

I have recently purshased D.T.P.
by P.C.G. Software and a scanner
would be a useful piece of
hardware to go along with it.
Maybe a review of D.T.P would be
welcomed in OUTLET in the future
when I have got to grips with it
a bit more.

I also, not long ago, bought an
LC-10 printer replacing my old
Brother M1009. It's a great
printer, considering it only
cost `143 - a lot less than my
Brother did(printer that is).The
only thing I didn't like about
it was it has no skip perforat-
ion facility like the Brother
did but has lots more going for
it to compensate.

How many of your readers, I
wonder, made the same mistake as
I did in thinking the organizers
might have got the ALL FORMAT
SHOW sorted out by now or maybe
that's unfair and it's just the
Spectrum is so old- fashioned
and out-of-date that exhibitors
don't bother to attend.

Maybe I should mention at this
stage that I am getting on for
40 years of age and maybe it's I
that am old-fashioned along
with my dearly-loved Spectrum.

I, for one, expect to see all
sorts of hardware on show at
exhibitions i.e.,disc drives and
interfaces like the Disciple/+D
Swiftdisk,mice, scanners, speech
boxes, music machines.I could go
on but I think you get the idea.

None of this was at the last
show nore any of the software we
OUTLET readers like to see. One
exception was S D SOFTWARE with
"Hackers' Workbench".Also there,
almost sharing the same stand,
was FORMAT (Bob Brenchley).

Without going on too much, the
Computer Entertainment Show was
no better -a bit more glossy and
more expensive and more games
and more games... Bring back the
ZX Micro Fairs - they had every-
thing these new shows don't.
Maybe old and new organizers
could get together and bring
back some of the magic.

Do keep up the great job you're
both doing with OUTLET. I always
look forward to it coming
through the letterbox and it's
such good value for the money
which is quite rare for lots of
software these days.

           Raymond Hoy

To Raymond Hoy from Brian Cavers

Your 128K has an RS232 port so,
in theory, you should be able to
attach most scanners. However, I
am not that experienced with the
hardware side of computing so I
hesitate lest I misdirect you.
Right, that's enough hesitation,
LION COMPUTERS,778 Borough Road,
Birkenhead, Merseyside, L42 9JG
(Tel:051 255 0625) offer the PC

`189.95.I recommend you ask them

to see if any of our readers can
help. I'd be interested to hear
if anyone has a scanner working
with a Spectrum. - Brian

From:Derek Morgan, LANCASHIRE.

Hi Ron, Brian,

Thanks for Issue 38 of OUTLET,
and for looking at my printer
problem.

I read with interest your review
of SAMTAPE 2, as I received
SAMTAPE 3, (the update), last
week , and the DTP part of it
didn't work, I thought I would
write and let the members know.

After reading in FORMAT, and the
SAM newsletter, that the SAM
version of PCG 'S DTP was just a
Spectrum emulator, I thought
that the SAMTAPE 3 upgrade at
`4.50, must be a better buy.

The tape came within four days.
The envelope contained the tape
and three sheets of A4 printed
info on how to use the NEW
version of the SAMTAPE and how
to convert your DESK TOP PUBLI-
SHER to run on SAM.

The three-page manual was up to
LERM'S usual standards:very easy
to follow. After loading from
tape, the program is saved to a
newly-formatted disc that I did
earlier, by pressing the F4 key.

The extra features of 'ST3' as
they call it, are an improvement
on 'ST2'. You can now change the
loading numbers to improve tape
loading and ROM1 or ROM2 will
be displayed on the main menu.

A new option on the menu is
shown under F6.This key will now
load any Spectrum program saved
on the Plus D or Disciple with
the SNAPSHOT button.


The program has the same bugs in
it as mentioned in OUTLET 38's
review. The program will display
an ERROR! and the keyboard will
lock up if you try and load a
NONE-snapshot program from plus-
D or Disciple disc. Snapshots
are loaded in by number, and not
by name,so ruling out the chance
of mis-spelling the program's
name and getting an error and
lockup.

The SCREEN$ SAVE option works
fine. When you are asked to name
your SCREEN$, you must start the
name with a # (hash). This saved
SCREEN$ may be reloaded in SAM
using MODE 1 and using the DUMP
command sent to the printer.


The information for converting
DTP is for tape, disc and micro-
drive versions. You need to con-
vert or rewrite the WORDMASTER
program, to make it swap from
Spectrum mode to SAM BASIC.There
is a small BASIC SAM program to
MERGE in and a KEYSCAN code file
to be saved before you save the
new WORDMASTER program to disc.

Keypress response/delay can be
adjusted from the SAM BASIC
loader. The auto-repeat was far
too fast for me so this was a
good thing.

You cannot use files created by
FLASH and some of the extension
files will not recognise the
cursor keys so you will have to
use the Spectrum SHIFT key plus
keys 5 to 8. Screen colours can
also be altered to taste, from a
procedure called "COLOURS".

There are some small BASIC
programs to help you copy the
extension files onto disc, and a
list of fonts and extension
files with their code length
shown for microdrive owners.

With the program up and running,
I tried to save a small file to
disc. It didn't work, I tried to
load in a font file. This didn't
work either.

I redid the conversion twice
before I rang Mr. LERM about my
problem. He informed me that the
DTP conversion didn't work with
all the versions of DTP. My
version, as listed in the
WORDMASTER manual, is a revised
manual version 2:September 1988.

Mr LERM said that he did not
have a copy of WORDMASTER as he
didn't use it. He offered to
look at my version/copy when he
had the time to see if he could
find the fault (after a bit of

persuasion that was) but as he
was very busy he didn't know
when this would be. He did
mention that he would have to
charge me a few pounds for this
service. I cannot send it back
and ask for a refund because
they do not give refunds on
upgraded tapes.

Did you know that DILWYN JONES
is writing a book for SAM on
computing? Bob (will he ever
read his mail) Brenchley, has
given Dilwyn a free hand with
the book to just what he wants.

              Derek

Should be interesting!Thanks for
the SAMTAPE info.
                  - Brian Cavers

From: Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS


Dear Ron & Brian

In Outletters 38, Chris Clayton
asked if there was a POKE to
make I/F1 'invisible'. Well no
doubt by now you will have been
snowed under with the solution
[er... you're the only snowflake
actually - BC] - but just in
case here is my 9-byte answer.
It can be stored anywhere above
ramtop, or in the printer buffer
so that the address will always
be known.

The 9 bytes are:-

42,79,92,17,182,92,195,229,25

An area that might be of use for
storing the code is the STREAMS
area from 23568-23605 inclusive.
Normally, with no extra channels
opened, locations 23582 to 23605
can hold a short code routine or
be used as a buffer etc. Since
it would be reasonable to assume
no more than another 5 channels
are to be opened (#4,5, 6,7,8)it
would leave 23592-23605 free for
your own use. Closing a channel
would not affect code but CLEAR#
would wipe it out.As the STREAMS
area does not wander around in
RAM, the address of your code
remains fixed whatever's fasten-
ed to the back of your Spectrum.
To be safe you could POKE those
9 bytes into 23597-23605 inclus-
ive and RAND USR 23597 will make
I/F 1 system variables vanish.

In the same issue, G.J. Owens
asked about a list of BBC & ILR
radio stations. Books that list
these are 'World Radio Handbook'
- excellent but pricey - or
'International Radio Station
Guide' by Bernard Publications
(BP255) at about `5.

Failing these, one can always
write to BBC engineering at
Broadcasting House and to the
IBA at Brompton Road, London for
fuller details on commercial
radio/tv stations.
                 Regards,

                  Malcolm


Many thanks! - Brian Cavers

From:Stephen Watson, E. KILBRIDE

Dear Ron and Brian,

Re: Mike Jones' letter in Issue 38, why bother with TASCON when with the assistance of the manual and OUTLET you can produce an excellent version of TASWORD 2 to run with the Plus D. I recently purchased TASWORD 2 and followed the instructions in the manual for the conversion to the microdrive version then ran the TAS-EXTRAS programme in OUTLET Issue 24.This should also meet J.W. Dear Ron & Brian

In Outletters 38, Chris Clayton asked if there was a POKE to make I/F1 'invisible'. Well no doubt by now you will have been snowed under with the solution [er... you're the only snowflake actually - BC] - but just in case here is my 9-byte answer. It can be stored anywhere above ramtop, or in the printer buffer so that the address will always be known.

The 9 bytes are:-

```text
42,79,92,17,182,92,195,229,25
```

An area that might be of use for storing the code is the STREAMS area from 23568-23605 inclusive. Normally, with no extra channels opened, locations 23582 to 23605 can hold a short code routine or be used as a buffer etc. Since it would be reasonable to assume no more than another 5 channels are to be opened (#4,5, 6,7,8)it would leave 23592-23605 free for your own use. Closing a channel would not affect code but CLEAR# would wipe it out.As the STREAMS area does not wander around in RAM, the address of your code remains fixed whatever's fasten- ed to the back of your Spectrum. To be safe you could POKE those 9 bytes into 23597-23605 inclus- ive and RAND USR 23597 will make I/F 1 system variables vanish.
